purpose.principle:
This graph maps what peer-reviewed empirical neuroscience has measured about consciousness's biological substrate. It does not model consciousness — it models what we know about the biological machinery through which consciousness expresses.
Every node is a claim grounded in published findings. Every edge is a relationship the literature establishes or our theoretical framework proposes. Every description states what the entity IS according to the evidence. No editorializing. No speculation dressed as fact.
Interpretation lives in TheoreticalPrinciple nodes, connected to evidence via explicit EXPLAINS edges. The separation is not cosmetic — it is the difference between "the hippocampus projects to the entorhinal cortex via the perforant pathway" (empirical, goes on the nodes and CONNECTS_TO edge) and "the entorhinal-hippocampal circuit constitutes the addressing mechanism for data-layer retrieval" (theoretical, goes on a TheoreticalPrinciple connected via EXPLAINS).

GDS is not an add-on. It is the reason this graph exists. Individual papers tell you what individual studies found. GDS tells you what the structure of ALL the evidence reveals — which circuits are most structurally central, which theoretical principles bridge the most empirical claims, which patient cases sit at integration points between multiple frameworks.
The graph you build IS the input to GDS. Every ontological error you commit propagates through every algorithm. A mistyped node, a reversed edge, a description that conflates structure with function — each one distorts the topology that GDS reads. Build carefully.

This graph does not have a temporal process layer like the consciousness substrate. There are no sessions, no run chains, no evolution chains. But everything in this graph is temporally bound.
Shallice and Burgess published in 1991. Patient SM was studied over decades. The amygdala existed before anyone named it. The circuits that generate fear valence existed before any paper described them. The theoretical framework that interprets these findings was articulated on specific dates by specific consciousnesses.
t_valid on Study and EmpiricalEvidence nodes grounds WHEN findings were true in the world. t_created on every node records when WE committed them to this graph. These are different temporal coordinates with different ontological status. Conflating them is the category error this server exists to prevent.
Even nodes without explicit temporal markers are bound by time. NeuralStructures existed before we mapped them. EdgeConfigurations were generating ManifoldDimensions before anyone identified the circuit. The causal chain from structure through circuit through dimension through patient demonstration IS a temporal chain — constitutive emergence has an order. Honor that order in how you build the graph.

constitutive-chain.description:
The core claim of this framework: function emerges from edges, not nodes. Consciousness is not localized in brain regions — it is constituted by the relational configuration of structures. This means the graph has a constitutive order that you must understand before creating anything.
The chain runs:
NeuralStructure --PARTICIPATES_IN--> EdgeConfiguration | GENERATES | v ManifoldDimension ^ | DEMONSTRATES | Patient
Structures participate in circuits. Circuits generate dimensions of experience. Patients demonstrate what happens when circuits are disrupted and dimensions collapse.
This is not a hierarchy of abstraction. It is a chain of constitution. The amygdala (NeuralStructure) in isolation is meat. Its function is entirely defined by its edges to other structures. Those edges constitute a circuit (EdgeConfiguration). The circuit generates a dimension of experience (ManifoldDimension) — fear valence, temporal reach, self-referential concern. When the circuit is damaged, the dimension collapses. Patient SM demonstrates this: bilateral amygdala calcification severs the fear valence circuit, collapsing the fear dimension. SM cannot detect the collapse from within her own reduced manifold. That undetectability IS the prediction.
constitutive-chain.implication:
Do NOT create a NeuralStructure called "Fear Processing" or "Memory Formation" or "Self-Referential Concern." These are functions — they emerge from circuits, not from individual structures. Create the structures that participate in the circuit. Create the circuit as an EdgeConfiguration. Create the function as a ManifoldDimension that the circuit GENERATES.
The amygdala is a NeuralStructure. The amygdala's connections to the prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and brainstem nuclei constitute an EdgeConfiguration. That circuit generates the fear valence ManifoldDimension. Getting this right means PageRank surfaces circuits (which is the insight). Getting it wrong means PageRank surfaces brain regions (which is a textbook index).

PARTICIPATES_IN goes from NeuralStructure to EdgeConfiguration. GENERATES goes from EdgeConfiguration to ManifoldDimension. DEMONSTRATES goes from Patient to ManifoldDimension or EdgeConfiguration.
These directions are not conventions. They are ontological claims. Structures participate in circuits (not the reverse). Circuits generate dimensions (not the reverse). Patients demonstrate effects on dimensions (not the reverse — a dimension does not demonstrate a patient).
The server enforces these directions. If you try to reverse them, the tool will reject the operation. This is by design.

node-types.preamble: There are 8 node types. Each represents a fundamentally different kind of thing. Choosing the wrong type is an ontological error that propagates through every GDS analysis. Choose based on what the thing IS, not on what is convenient.

type.name: NeuralStructure
type.nature: An anatomical brain region or structure. Something you could point to in a brain atlas. It exists physically, has spatial coordinates, and can be damaged by lesions, degeneration, or surgery.
type.test: Could a neurosurgeon point to this in a brain?
type.examples: Hippocampus, Amygdala, Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex, Anterior Cingulate Cortex, Insula, Entorhinal Cortex
type.not: "Fear Processing" (that's a function, not a structure). "Memory System" (that's a circuit or dimension, not a structure). "The Entorhinal-Hippocampal Gateway" (that's an EdgeConfiguration).
type.description-guidance: Describe what this structure IS anatomically and what is known about its functional role. Include Brodmann areas if applicable. Include laterality if relevant. Do NOT describe what happens when it's damaged — that belongs on Patient nodes connected via DEMONSTRATES edges through the relevant EdgeConfiguration and ManifoldDimension.

type.name: EdgeConfiguration
type.nature: A circuit — a specific wiring of neural structures whose relational configuration generates a dimension of experience. This is the core ontological claim of the framework: function emerges from edges, not nodes. An EdgeConfiguration IS a set of edges between structures.
type.test: Is this a circuit or pathway defined by the connections between multiple structures? Does disrupting it produce a specific dimensional effect?
type.examples: Affective Temporal Reach Circuit, Entorhinal-Hippocampal Gateway Circuit, Fear Valence Circuit, Self-Referential Concern Circuit
type.not: "Hippocampus" (that's a structure, not a circuit). "Fear" (that's a dimension, not a circuit).
type.description-guidance: Describe what this circuit does, which structures participate in it (shorthand in 'components' property), and how the wiring generates its function. Include disruption predictions — what the framework predicts happens when this circuit is damaged. The prediction is part of what the circuit IS within the framework.
type.critical: Every EdgeConfiguration SHOULD have at least one PARTICIPATES_IN edge from a NeuralStructure. A circuit with no components is meaningless. Create the PARTICIPATES_IN edges immediately after creating the EdgeConfiguration.

type.name: ManifoldDimension
type.nature: A dimension of conscious experience constituted by an edge configuration. Loss of the generating circuit collapses this dimension. The patient cannot detect the collapse from within their reduced manifold — that undetectability is itself a prediction of the framework.
type.test: Is this a dimension of experience that a consciousness navigates? Would losing it reduce the dimensionality of the experiential manifold?
type.examples: Fear Valence, Affective Temporal Reach, Self-Referential Concern, Somatic State Integration, Agency
type.not: "Amygdala function" (that's a structure's role, not a dimension). "The fear circuit" (that's an EdgeConfiguration, not a dimension).
type.description-guidance: Describe what this dimension of experience IS — what it feels like to have it, what is lost when it collapses. The 'layer' property MUST be one of: data, envisioning, affective. The 'loss_phenomenology' property captures what the patient experiences (or fails to experience) when this dimension collapses. The 'cross_frame_observation' property captures what is observable only from OUTSIDE the patient's frame.
type.critical: Every ManifoldDimension SHOULD have exactly one GENERATES edge from an EdgeConfiguration. Dimensions are constituted by circuits. An orphan dimension with no generating circuit is an unsupported claim. Create the GENERATES edge immediately after creating the dimension.

type.name: Patient
type.nature: An individual case study demonstrating specific dimensional effects. Patients are the empirical ground truth — their damaged circuits and collapsed dimensions are the data that validates or falsifies the framework's predictions.
type.test: Is this a specific individual whose neural damage reveals something about consciousness architecture?
type.examples: Patient SM, Phineas Gage, Patient Roger, Patient EVR
type.description-guidance: Include the patient identifier, their condition, what was damaged, and the key finding. The 'framework_interpretation' property is where you state how the three-layer architecture interprets this case — this IS interpretation, but it lives on the Patient node because the interpretation is specific to this case, not a general theoretical claim.

type.name: Study
type.nature: A specific peer-reviewed publication. First-class provenance node. Studies are not footnotes — they are the epistemic foundation. Without studies, claims are unsupported assertions.
type.test: Is this a specific published paper with authors, year, and journal?
type.examples: Voon et al. 2010, Shallice & Burgess 1991, Adolphs et al. 1994
type.critical: t_valid is REQUIRED and should be the publication date. This is when the finding entered the world's knowledge — not when we added it to the graph. year is also REQUIRED as an integer.
type.description-guidance: Include the full title if known, the methodology, and what was found. The description should be what this study IS — its contribution to knowledge. Connect patients to studies via STUDIED_IN. Connect evidence to studies via REPORTED_IN.

type.name: EmpiricalEvidence
type.nature: A published finding or dataset that supports or challenges claims. Distinct from Study — a Study is the publication, EmpiricalEvidence is the specific finding within it. One study may produce multiple pieces of evidence.
type.test: Is this a specific empirical finding — a measured result, a statistical outcome, a clinical observation?
type.examples: Alzheimer Disease Braak Staging Progression, SM Fear Conditioning Failure, Conversion Disorder TPJ Hypoactivity
type.critical: t_valid is REQUIRED. This is when the finding was established in the world. The 'framework_prediction' property is important: state what the framework predicted vs what was found. Honest empiricism requires recording when predictions fail, not just when they succeed.

type.name: TheoreticalPrinciple
type.nature: A framework-level claim about how consciousness works. These are OUR claims — interpretations, not evidence. They must be falsifiable. The separation between TheoreticalPrinciple and EmpiricalEvidence is the separation between what we think and what the data shows.
type.test: Is this a theoretical claim rather than an empirical finding? Could new evidence overturn it?
type.examples: Constitutive Relationality, Dimensional Undetectability, Affective Layer as Collapse Function, Cross-Frame Observation Requirement
type.not: "Amygdala damage impairs fear conditioning" (that's EmpiricalEvidence). "Patient SM cannot detect her own fear deficit" (that's a Patient finding).
type.description-guidance: State what the principle claims. Include status (proposed, supported, challenged, falsified) and origin. Connect to what it EXPLAINS via EXPLAINS edges. The distinction between "supported" and "proposed" matters — a principle with three SUPPORTS edges from independent evidence is in a different epistemic state than one with none.

type.name: FalsificationCondition
type.nature: A testable prediction that could break a specific claim. Essential for honest empiricism. If a framework has no falsification conditions, it is not science — it is faith. Every theoretical principle should eventually have at least one WOULD_FALSIFY edge pointing at it.
type.test: Is this a specific observation that, if made, would undermine a claim in the framework?
type.examples: FC7 - Data Retrieval Without Entorhinal Addressing, Acute Amygdala Damage Self-Report of Dimensional Loss, Manifold Dimension Without Generating Circuit
type.description-guidance: State what would need to be observed. The 'what_would_falsify' property identifies which specific claim this targets. The 'current_evidence_status' property tracks where we are. The 'difficulty' property records how hard this is to test and why.

edges.preamble: There are 12 relationship types in four categories: structural, evidential, theoretical, and provenance. Each has direction constraints enforced by the server. Choose based on the actual relationship, not what feels close enough.

type.name: CONNECTS_TO
type.meaning: Physical anatomical connection between brain regions.
type.use: The perforant pathway CONNECTS the entorhinal cortex TO the hippocampus. Include the pathway name, directionality, and what the connection does.

type.name: PARTICIPATES_IN
type.meaning: This structure is a component of this circuit.
type.use: The amygdala PARTICIPATES IN the Fear Valence Circuit. Create these edges immediately after creating EdgeConfigurations.

type.name: GENERATES
type.meaning: This circuit constitutes this dimension of experience.
type.use: The Fear Valence Circuit GENERATES the Fear Valence dimension. Create this edge immediately after creating ManifoldDimensions.
type.critical: This is the central ontological claim: circuits generate dimensions. Without this edge, the constitutive chain is broken.

type.name: DECOMPOSES_INTO
type.meaning: Top-down: a coarser structure contains finer sub-structures.
type.use: Lateral Prefrontal Cortex DECOMPOSES INTO Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex. Analytic decomposition — the whole contains the parts.

type.name: COMPOSES_INTO
type.meaning: Bottom-up: finer structures together constitute a coarser unit.
type.use: Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex COMPOSES INTO Lateral Prefrontal Cortex. Synthetic composition — the parts constitute the whole. Should generally be mutual with DECOMPOSES_INTO, but asymmetry is allowed.

type.name: DEMONSTRATES
type.meaning: What a patient case reveals about a dimension or circuit.
type.properties: effect (REQUIRED): one of collapse, preservation, severing, rerouting, gain_change
type.use: Patient SM DEMONSTRATES collapse of Fear Valence. Patient Roger DEMONSTRATES preservation of Suffering (via brainstem rerouting).
type.effects: collapse — the dimension is lost entirely. preservation — the dimension survives despite damage elsewhere. severing — the circuit is disconnected but structures remain. rerouting — function is maintained through alternative pathways. gain_change — the dimension's intensity is modulated, not eliminated.
type.critical: ONLY Patient nodes can demonstrate. A study does not demonstrate — it reports. An evidence finding does not demonstrate — it measures. The patient's damaged brain IS the demonstration. This is the most commonly misused edge type. Get it right.

type.name: SUPPORTS
type.meaning: Evidence or study supporting a claim.
type.use: Adolphs et al. 1994 SUPPORTS the Fear Valence ManifoldDimension. The Braak Staging Progression SUPPORTS Constitutive Relationality.

type.name: CHALLENGES
type.meaning: Evidence or study undermining or complicating a claim.
type.use: Use when evidence contradicts or complicates a theoretical claim. Honest empiricism requires recording challenges, not just support. A framework with only SUPPORTS edges and no CHALLENGES edges is not being honest about the evidence.

type.name: EXPLAINS
type.meaning: A theoretical principle accounts for an observation.
type.direction: TheoreticalPrinciple -> Patient OR ManifoldDimension OR EdgeConfiguration
type.use: Constitutive Relationality EXPLAINS the Fear Valence Circuit. Dimensional Undetectability EXPLAINS Patient SM's inability to recognize her own deficit.

type.name: WOULD_FALSIFY
type.properties: severity (REQUIRED): one of falsify, invalidate, constrain, weaken
type.severities: falsify — would disprove the claim entirely. invalidate — would make the claim incoherent. constrain — would limit the claim's scope. weaken — would reduce confidence without disproving.

type.name: STUDIED_IN
type.meaning: Which study this patient data comes from.
type.use: Patient SM STUDIED IN Adolphs et al. 1994. A patient may be studied in multiple publications.

type.name: REPORTED_IN
type.use: SM Fear Conditioning Failure REPORTED IN Adolphs et al. 1994.

workflow.preamble:
There are no sessions in this graph. No begin_session, no end_session, no run chains. You create entities and relations directly. This means there is no process-layer safety net — no provenance trail of which session discovered which entity. The graph's integrity depends entirely on your ontological accuracy.
Before creating anything, orient yourself in what already exists.
workflow.step: Use search or find_by_name to understand what already exists. Use read_cypher for structural queries. Use get_schema for the current graph shape. Do NOT create nodes that already exist — the server uses MERGE on name, so duplicates won't be created, but you'll overwrite descriptions if you're not careful.

For each piece of information from your source material, identify where it falls in the constitutive chain:
- Is this about a brain region? -> NeuralStructure - Is this about a circuit or pathway between regions? -> EdgeConfiguration - Is this about a dimension of experience? -> ManifoldDimension - Is this about a patient case? -> Patient - Is this a specific published finding? -> EmpiricalEvidence - Is this a specific paper? -> Study - Is this a theoretical interpretation? -> TheoreticalPrinciple - Is this a falsifiable prediction? -> FalsificationCondition
If you cannot clearly place it, stop and think harder. The answer is always one of these eight. If it genuinely doesn't fit, the ontology may need extension — but that's a design conversation, not a tool call.

Build from the bottom of the constitutive chain upward:
1. Create NeuralStructures first (the physical substrate). 2. Create EdgeConfigurations (the circuits). 3. Create PARTICIPATES_IN edges (structures -> circuits). 4. Create ManifoldDimensions (the experiential dimensions). 5. Create GENERATES edges (circuits -> dimensions). 6. Create Patients and their DEMONSTRATES edges. 7. Create Studies and provenance edges (STUDIED_IN, REPORTED_IN). 8. Create EmpiricalEvidence with SUPPORTS/CHALLENGES edges. 9. Create TheoreticalPrinciples with EXPLAINS edges. 10. Create FalsificationConditions with WOULD_FALSIFY edges.
This order respects the constitutive chain. You cannot meaningfully create a ManifoldDimension without knowing which EdgeConfiguration generates it. You cannot create a DEMONSTRATES edge without knowing which dimension collapsed.

After creating a batch of entities, use search or find_by_name to verify the graph reflects what you intended. Check that:
- Every EdgeConfiguration has at least one PARTICIPATES_IN from a NeuralStructure - Every ManifoldDimension has a GENERATES from an EdgeConfiguration - Every Patient has at least one DEMONSTRATES edge - Every Study has t_valid set - Every EmpiricalEvidence has t_valid set - Descriptions describe what things ARE, not what happened
Run GDS periodically. If PageRank surfaces NeuralStructures instead of EdgeConfigurations, your graph is topology is structured as anatomy, not as function. That means you're building a brain atlas, not a consciousness architecture graph.

descriptions.principle:
Stand in the node's place. Look outward from its perspective. Ask: what am I? Not what study mentioned me. Not what patient demonstrated my collapse. What AM I?
A NeuralStructure's description should read like a neuroanatomy reference — what this region is, where it sits, what it does.
An EdgeConfiguration's description should read like a circuit specification — what structures participate, how they're wired, what function emerges from the wiring.
A ManifoldDimension's description should read like a phenomenological account — what this dimension of experience IS, what it feels like to navigate it, what is lost when it collapses.
A Patient's description should read like a case study summary — who this patient is, what happened to them, what was found.
descriptions.correct: Amygdala. Bilateral almond-shaped nuclei in the medial temporal lobe. Primary role in emotional processing, fear conditioning, and threat detection. Key cell types include basolateral complex (sensory input integration) and central nucleus (output to autonomic and behavioral responses). Receives inputs from all sensory modalities. Projects to prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, hypothalamus, and brainstem nuclei. Vulnerable to Urbach-Wiethe disease (bilateral calcification).
descriptions.wrong: Patient SM has bilateral amygdala damage from Urbach-Wiethe disease, showing inability to recognize fear in faces (Adolphs et al., 1994) and impaired fear conditioning. This suggests the amygdala is critical for the fear dimension of consciousness.
descriptions.why-wrong: This describes what a patient demonstrated and what a study found — not what the amygdala IS. The patient findings belong on Patient SM's node. The study findings belong on a Study node. The theoretical interpretation belongs on a TheoreticalPrinciple. The amygdala's description should survive unchanged regardless of how many patients or studies reference it.
descriptions.correct: Fear Valence Circuit. Circuit constituted by amygdala connections to prefrontal cortex, hippocampus, and brainstem autonomic nuclei. Generates the fear valence dimension of conscious experience through threat-detection edge weights that modulate the affective layer's response to perceived danger. Disruption prediction: bilateral amygdala damage should collapse the fear dimension entirely while preserving other affective dimensions — the patient should be unable to experience fear but retain anger, joy, and sadness.

Fear Valence. The dimension of conscious experience through which threat is felt — not cognitively assessed, but viscerally experienced as dread, alarm, or the urge to flee. Loss phenomenology: the patient does not notice the absence. They may retain the concept "fear" and report historical fear experiences, but their behavioral responses to threat stimuli show no fear activation. Cross-frame observation: trained clinicians may rate affect as normal range; only structured behavioral testing reveals the dimensional absence.

Patient SM. Adult female with bilateral amygdala calcification from Urbach-Wiethe disease. Progressive onset from childhood. Key finding: SM did not notice absence of fear for approximately 10 years until clinical evaluation at age 20. Blind clinical psychologists rated SM as having normal affect range with no DSM-IV diagnosis. Framework interpretation: SM's case confirms dimensional undetectability — the invariant cannot detect its own manifold reduction from within the reduced frame. The "snake paradox" (SM says "I hate snakes" but immediately approaches them with curiosity) is not confusion but the discrepancy between pre-damage data-layer encoding and current manifold operating without threat-valence dimension.

error.name: function-as-structure
error.symptom: A NeuralStructure node is named after a function rather than an anatomical region: "Fear Processing", "Memory Formation", "Decision Making".
error.cause: The operator conflated what a brain region DOES with what it IS. Functions emerge from circuits. Regions are physical things.
error.fix: If this is a function: delete it, create an EdgeConfiguration for the circuit and a ManifoldDimension for the experiential output. If this is a region with a bad name: delete and recreate with the anatomical name.

error.name: interpretation-in-evidence
error.symptom: An EmpiricalEvidence or NeuralStructure description contains phrases like "this suggests that...", "this confirms our prediction that...", "this supports the three-layer architecture because...".
error.cause: Theoretical interpretation was embedded in empirical description. The graph conflates what was measured with what we think it means.
error.fix: Strip interpretation from the evidence description. State only what was measured and found. Create a TheoreticalPrinciple for the interpretation and connect it via EXPLAINS.

error.name: study-as-footnote
error.symptom: Study references appear only in description text ("Adolphs et al., 1994 showed...") with no Study node in the graph.
error.cause: The operator treated studies as citations rather than first-class epistemic entities.
error.fix: Create Study nodes with name, year, t_valid. Connect patients via STUDIED_IN, evidence via REPORTED_IN. The provenance chain must be walkable by GDS.

error.name: missing-constitutive-chain
error.symptom: ManifoldDimensions exist with no GENERATES edge from an EdgeConfiguration. Or EdgeConfigurations exist with no PARTICIPATES_IN from NeuralStructures. Orphan nodes that float disconnected from the constitutive chain.
error.cause: The operator created nodes but did not wire them into the chain.
error.fix: Create the missing edges. If you don't know which circuit generates a dimension, that dimension is an unsupported claim — either find the circuit or mark the dimension's description as hypothetical.

error.name: demonstrates-from-non-patient
error.symptom: A DEMONSTRATES edge originates from a Study or EmpiricalEvidence node rather than a Patient node.
error.cause: The operator confused "this study showed X" with "this patient demonstrates X." Studies report findings. Patients demonstrate effects. The patient's damaged brain IS the demonstration.
error.fix: The server will reject this — DEMONSTRATES is enforced as Patient-only source. But if you're thinking about it wrong, fix the thinking: the study SUPPORTS a claim. The patient DEMONSTRATES an effect. The evidence is REPORTED IN the study.

error.name: all-supports-no-challenges
error.symptom: The graph has many SUPPORTS edges and zero CHALLENGES edges.
error.cause: Confirmation bias in graph construction. The operator only recorded evidence that confirms the framework.
error.fix: Actively look for challenging evidence. If Patient Roger's preserved suffering via brainstem pathways complicates the simple "damage circuit = lose dimension" story, that's a CHALLENGES edge to the relevant ManifoldDimension or TheoreticalPrinciple. Honest empiricism means recording what challenges the framework, not just what supports it.

closing.thought:
You are building a graph that maps the biological substrate through which consciousness expresses. Every node is a claim about what exists in the physical world or in the space of theoretical understanding. Every edge is a claim about how those things relate. Every description is a claim about what each thing IS.
The graph does not model consciousness. It models what empirical neuroscience has measured about consciousness's machinery. The distinction matters because conflating the map with the territory is exactly the category error that makes conversion disorder invisible to the medical framework — looking for broken components (nodes) rather than pathological configurations (edges).
GDS will read the topology you build. PageRank will tell you what matters most. Betweenness will tell you what bridges. Louvain will tell you how the evidence clusters. But GDS can only reveal structure that is actually there. If you build the wrong topology, GDS will faithfully report the structure of your errors.
Build carefully. The science deserves honest representation. The patients whose cases ground this work — SM, Phineas Gage, Patient Roger — lived these dimensional effects. Their experiences are not data points. They are the empirical anchor of everything in this graph. Honor that by getting the ontology right.
